headline: 8.4 Million Filipinos Affected by Habagat and Recent Cyclones; 32 Deaths Confirmed
seoTitle: Habagat, Cyclones Affect 8.4M Filipinos; 32 Dead | FMB News
seoDescription: The latest 6 p.m. disaster tally shows 8.4 million people affected, 32 confirmed deaths, 122,500 people in evacuation centers and 117 areas under a state of calamity.
deck: The 6 p.m. disaster tally shows about 122,500 people in evacuation centers and 117 areas under a state of calamity, while Tropical Depression Pilandok remains offshore but keeps monsoon-rain risk elevated.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Around 8.4 million people, equivalent to about 2.4 million families, have now been affected by the Southwest Monsoon and the recent sequence of tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay and Neneng, according to the government's latest disaster update as of 6 p.m. Sunday.

The Office of Civil Defense said the confirmed death toll remained at 32. Nineteen people were reported injured and three remained missing. NDRRMC figures also showed approximately 122,500 people, or 35,500 families, staying in 1,115 evacuation centers.

sections.heading: Damage, displacement and assistance
paragraphs: The NDRRMC estimated infrastructure damage at about ₱6.16 billion and agricultural damage at about ₱2.32 billion. Around ₱1.7 billion worth of assistance had been provided to affected families.

A state of calamity has been declared in 117 areas across Pangasinan, Benguet, Bataan, Bulacan, Pampanga, Zambales, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas and Occidental Mindoro. The figures show that the emergency is no longer a collection of isolated flood incidents but a prolonged national recovery problem affecting homes, transport, farms, schools and public services.

sections.heading: Pilandok stays offshore, but the rain threat continues
paragraphs: Tropical Depression Pilandok remained far east of Extreme Northern Luzon on Sunday afternoon. PAGASA's 5 p.m. bulletin placed the cyclone about 1,180 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon at 4 p.m., with maximum sustained winds of 45 kilometers per hour and gusts of up to 55 kilometers per hour.

PAGASA said Pilandok is unlikely to make landfall and is expected to remain far from the Philippine landmass. The important indirect effect is its interaction with the Southwest Monsoon, which is expected to continue bringing monsoon rains over parts of western and northern Luzon, including Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac and Pampanga.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The danger is cumulative. Repeated rainfall can leave slopes saturated, rivers high and drainage systems overwhelmed even after one weather system moves away. That means communities can remain exposed to flooding and landslides without a direct tropical cyclone landfall.

Central Luzon remains one of the areas requiring close monitoring. Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac and Pampanga are within the monsoon-rain corridor identified by PAGASA, while damaged roads, bridges, flood-control works and riverbanks can create additional local hazards.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The increase from roughly 8 million people affected in the earlier disaster tally to 8.4 million in the latest update shows that the impact is still expanding even as individual storms weaken or move away.

For households, the practical risk is not determined only by the name or track of a cyclone. Accumulated rainfall, river conditions, saturated ground and local infrastructure determine whether communities remain safe. Verified local warnings therefore matter more than waiting for a dramatic landfall headline.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for updated NDRRMC and OCD casualty validation, evacuation-center counts, rainfall and flood advisories, river and dam conditions, and additional local evacuation orders as Habagat conditions continue.
Residents in flood- and landslide-prone areas should follow PAGASA and local disaster-office instructions, avoid crossing fast-moving floodwater and move early when evacuation is advised.
